data.name: Mainu
data.gender_notes: Mainu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'ma' meaning 'mother' and 'anu' meaning 'little', Mainu signifies 'little one' or 'beloved child'. In Hindu mythology, Mainu is a term of endearment for the goddess Parvati, who is known as the mother of Lord Shiva. The name Mainu carries the meaning “Little One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mainu usually hope their child will grow to embody little one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of maternal love and care.
data.etymology: Mainu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mainu total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mainu has a rich and diverse cultural significance in Hindu Society. It is a term of endearment and signifies love, caring, and nurturing, aligning with the values placed on family and motherhood in Hindu culture. The name is also associated with sacred mother goddesses such as Parvati, Lakshmi, and Saraswati, who embody the divine feminine and are revered for their love, grace, and nurturing qualities.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Mainu holds profound meaning, signifying the protective and nurturing nature of the Divine and the important role of mothers and caregivers in our lives. It serves as a reminder of the divine love, grace, and compassion that flows through all of us and instills values of love, compassion, and caring in those who bear this name. Mainu is also an invitation to connect with the divine feminine through motherhood, nurturing, and caring for others, ultimately fostering spiritual growth and self-realization.
